entries.label: Environment
entries.effect: The cluster's environment (dev, stg, prd). A production token here makes the cluster protected even without protected: true.
entries.save: Review and apply in Fleet writes the changed fields into the cluster's entry in fleet.yaml, every other line as written, then uses them. A hand edit of the entry takes effect through "Use the file's values".

entries.label: Kubeconfig

entries.label: Protection
entries.effect: A protected cluster asks for a typed confirmation before every destructive verb, and keeps its context from an off-machine AI unless protected-cluster egress is allowed. It is also inferred from a prd, prod or production token in the environment, name or context; this flag makes it explicit, and false never removes an inferred protection.
entries.save: Review and apply in Fleet writes the changed fields into the cluster's entry in fleet.yaml, every other line as written, then uses them. A hand edit of the entry takes effect through "Use the file's values".

entries.label: Tags
entries.effect: Free labels shown on the cluster and used for grouping. tags.env is read as the environment when environment is unset; a tag named like a cluster field is warned about, since it sets nothing.
entries.save: Review and apply in Fleet writes the changed fields into the cluster's entry in fleet.yaml, every other line as written, then uses them. A hand edit of the entry takes effect through "Use the file's values".

entries.label: Allow protected-cluster egress
entries.effect: Send protected (prd) clusters' context to the AI in use. One permission for chat, Explain, Suggest-fix and investigations, and it follows whichever provider and origin are in use: it stays on if you change them later. Off: AI stays unavailable on protected clusters unless the model runs on this machine.
entries.validation: true or false; turning it on asks you to type a confirmation, and saves.
entries.test: Test sends one short request to the provider in use, with this draft.
entries.save: Save rewrites fleet.yaml's ai block (comments inside it are not kept) and rebuilds the AI in use.
